data.head: Fault-identity semantics decided — fingerprint normalization and incident dedupe agree on when two faults are one (operator-directed 2026-08-16 at the 0-pending adaptation wrap; evidence: `conductor/conductor-0.2.0/chunks/2026-08-15-*/` + `2026-08-16-*/`, all measured against this repo's HEAD d090314; that repo is READ-ONLY from here — cite, never copy) · TWO LAYERS, ONE QUESTION — what makes two faults the same fault: (a) FINGERPRINT identity — `is_absolute_path_start` fires on ANY `/`, so in effect only the LEADING path segment stays identity-significant, while the module doc and an inline comment both claim absolute-paths-only; distinct faults can therefore over-coalesce into a single storm. Decide the intended semantic FIRST, then align impl or docs to it — never infer the intent from current behaviour. (b) INCIDENT identity — dedupe keys on an OPEN incident, NOT on the fingerprint: while one is open a storm carrying a DIFFERENT fingerprint is absorbed into it (`created:false` / `deduped:true` — a deliberately unique-typed canary deduped anyway), with the ~5min auto-resolve window the only same-data-dir cure. The design question: should a distinct-fingerprint storm open a second concurrent incident? · WHY IT PRECEDES P-075/P-076: both assert on incident formation and read-back, so their acceptances encode whatever fault-identity means; settling it first writes them once against decided semantics instead of encoding today's measured-but-undecided behaviour into two suites
data.desc: Fault-identity semantics decided — both layers ANSWERED, and a third premise inverted. Incident identity stays COALESCE-PER-CUE-IDENTITY on `(kind, scope, scope_id)` — now decided and pinned rather than incidental, with keying on the model-authored `L4Output.fingerprint` rejected (a constant under the deterministic runner) and the `AttentionCue` threading deferred. data.desc: Webview self-verify on the Windows host — an agent now presses a real control in the live Tauri window and the app's OWN record is the verdict: `cargo xtask webview-drive` drives the production custom-titlebar ✕ via tauri-driver + WebdriverIO and asserts `ui.layout.transition {layout_mode_from: compact-widget, layout_mode_to: hidden}` out of the obs log, because a press that "returned without throwing" proves nothing — the ACL drops a webview IPC silently, which is exactly the dead-affordance mode this closes. BOTH driver shapes were probed before either was built, per directive: (a) tauri-driver + WebdriverIO WON on measurement and owes no amendment; (b) CDP + Playwright attaches fine (all four windows enumerable) but has no CDP path at HEAD and runs against test-plan §2, so it was recorded and declined — `playwright.config.ts` left untouched and still inert. The directive's premise needed ONE correction that changed what the leg proves: `core:window:allow-close` is granted today, so the ✕ WORKS and the leg is a REGRESSION GUARD, not a bug repro — which is precisely why the mutation check was mandatory rather than prudent. Proven both directions: GREEN presses and logs the transition with a clean log (0 ERROR / 0 panic); RED, with the grant revoked and rebuilt, still FINDS and still PRESSES the button while the transition never appears — a naive "button exists and click didn't throw" check would have passed there. Needed no new obs target and no new allowlist leaf (`ui.layout.transition` already permitted every field, and `layout_mode_from` names which window closed for free). Recorded honestly as its own residual: the RED arm is MANUAL — only `--expect-absent` is code — so "capabilities/default.json byte-identical after restore" is a DISCIPLINE, and no shipped gate catches a left-revoked grant; tracked as a test-plan trigger, a CARRY on the Staged-bindings entry, and a harness rule.
